summary:
Silent Guardians of Space" is an interactive 3D browser-based museum and educational tool showcasing historical NASA hardware and scientific artifacts left on the Moon and Mars (rovers, landers, lunar rovers).

How it solves the problem: Modern teenagers often know only about active missions, while past spacecraft are tucked away in dry, jargon-heavy textbooks. The project merges a modern web tech stack (Three.js, WebGL), verified NASA catalog data, and generative AI to transform dry engineering metrics into emotional, first-person monologues from the artifacts themselves. Users can freely rotate textured 3D planets, explore exact landing coordinates via clickable markers, and view archival photos.

Why it is important: The project bridges the gap between complex scientific archives and a younger audience. It transforms the study of astronomy and physics into an engaging, interactive experience, bringing the forgotten history of space exploration to life and inspiring the next generation of engineers and researchers.
details:
"Silent Guardians of Space" is an interactive 3D browser-based web museum that brings abandoned NASA hardware on the Moon and Mars (rovers, landers) back to life.

  • How it works: Users rotate 3D planets featuring photorealistic textures, explore exact landing coordinates verified against NASA catalogs, and open info cards containing archival photos and emotional, first-person robotic "monologues." Clicking "Listen to Signal" plays real-time synthesized telemetry radio static.
  • Tech Stack: HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, Three.js (WebGL), Web Audio API, and generative AI (for crafting first-person storytelling).
  • Impact: The project bridges the gap between dry scientific archives and youth, turning astronomy into an engaging, accessible experience for students and STEM educators
